originalTitle: HomePod Mini 2 first look: Three things I love and one disappointment
summary: When I first heard about the new $149 HomePod Mini 2 at Apple's Welcome Home event last month, I was disappointed. content: When I first heard about the new $149 HomePod Mini 2 at Apple’s Welcome Home event last month, I was disappointed. It’s been six years since Apple launched its entry-level smart speaker, and all it got in the second gen was a chip bump, some color glowy stuff, and better AirPlay? For $50 more than the original, which launched at $99, Apple didn’t even upgrade the sound system. It felt like the company phoned this one in. Now that I’ve got my hands on a couple and set them up in my home office, I’m more enthused. The Mini 2 is so much faster than the first-gen Mini, playing music in a few seconds and responding to smart home commands just as quickly. If you’re fed up with standing over your HomePod waiting for it to finally do what you asked, then that alone is worth the upgrade. Here are my three favorite features of the new Mini 2 after spending a couple days with it, and my one big disappointment. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268839_HomePod_mini_2_JTuohy_0015.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Siri is much snappier and much less chatty The biggest upgrade for the Mini 2 is Siri AI, but that isn’t available yet. Apple says it’s coming “later” in a software update. However, the basic smart voice assistant has definitely improved. Siri on the Mini 2 is much snappier than on the first-gen Mini, regularly responding in under three seconds. This is thanks to a newer, faster processor (the S10, up from the S5) and Wi-Fi 6E support (up from Wi-Fi 4). When I asked Siri to play Taylor Swift, a song started in a couple of seconds. It correctly told me who won this year’s World Series in under two seconds, and turned off the light or opened the shades in under three seconds. [Video: HomePod Mini2 vs Mini 1 smart home speed] That’s a huge improvement over the up to 10 seconds I often have to wait for Siri to get things done on the first-gen Mini. However, asking something harder, like who will win the US midterm elections, still brings up the familiar offer to look at some web results on my iPhone. As I said, Siri AI isn’t here yet. The other new behavior I am really enjoying is that when I ask Siri to perform a smart home action, such as open the shades or turn on the lights, instead of “OK, Jen,” or “One sec,” followed by a wordy confirmation of the action that I often get on the first-gen Mini, the Mini 2 just does it and doesn’t talk back. It’s not silent for every action, but it’s quiet enough to be a noticeable improvement. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268839_HomePod_mini_2_JTuohy_0014.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] This Mini is gorgeous in green and sounds great The green color is divine. This is the prettiest small smart speaker I’ve seen — and I’ve tried them all. Yes, Amazon’s Echo Dot Max’s purple is fun, the Google Home Speaker’s pale green is elegant, but Apple’s deep green is seriously sophisticated. It’s a color that fits in really well in various places around my home, and I’m so glad the company finally released a green option. It’s a big improvement over the slightly garish yellow and orange of the prior-gen Minis and the best of the new colors. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268839_HomePod_mini_2_JTuohy_0003.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268839_HomePod_mini_2_JTuohy_0004.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] I saw all the colors in person at Apple’s Welcome Home event, and while the pink is pretty, it’s very pale, and the blue is functionally identical to the first-gen blue, maybe a shade lighter. While a lot of folks will be happy with black (don’t get white unless you plan to dust it regularly), the green is my new go-to. [Video: HomePod Mini 2 vs Mini 1 Sound Test] Two green HomePod Mini 2s look so good on the walnut Nanoleaf monitor stand I’m testing; it’s like my office got an instant upgrade. And while Apple didn’t update the speakers in the Mini 2, it’s still a very good speaker for its size, doing a fine job with Bad Bunny’s bass and delivering clear mids and vocals. While $300 is steep for computer speakers, two as a stereo pair in my office definitely delivered on room-filling sound. You can finally disable touch A few weeks ago I fumbled for my phone on my nightstand and accidentally hit the top of my HomePod Mini, blaring music in the bedroom at 3AM. My husband was not happy. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6666.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6661.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] A new setting in the Home app now lets you lock the Mini’s top controls. This goes for all HomePods, old and new, and it’s a major quality-of-life upgrade. How often do you intentionally touch the top of your HomePod? I bet far less often than accidentally! The other new trick for the top of the HomePod is Sound Glow. This makes the LEDs display colors that match the album art of the song you’re playing (it’s also backward compatible with the first-gen Mini and the second-gen HomePod). It’s neat, but only works with Apple Music and Podcasts and is so subtle that I don’t feel it adds much to my music-listening experience. [Image: A stereo pair of Minis sounds very good. Here they’re pictured on Nanoleaf’s new monitor stand, which has built-in LED lighting. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268839_HomePod_mini_2_JTuohy_0006.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Signature feature fail Beyond the speed improvement, the other new feature I was excited about is the HomePod Mini 2’s ability to be the default speaker for your Mac using what Apple calls “a responsive and persistent AirPlay connection.” This creates a wireless point-to-point connection between the computer and the HomePod. You can pair a single speaker or a stereo pair to your Mac, and the feature also works with the second-gen HomePod.
chineseTitle: HomePod Mini 2 第一眼看：三样我喜欢，一样令人失望
chineseSummary: 当我上个月在 Apple 欢迎回家活动中第一次听说售价 149 美元的新款 HomePod Mini 2 时，我感到很失望。距离苹果推出入门级智能音箱已有六年了，第二代的一切只是芯片凸起、一些彩色发光的东西和更好的 AirPlay？比 [...] 多 50 美元
chineseContent: 当我上个月在 Apple 欢迎回家活动中第一次听说售价 149 美元的新款 HomePod Mini 2 时，我感到很失望。距离苹果推出入门级智能音箱已有六年了，第二代的一切只是芯片凸起、一些彩色发光的东西和更好的 AirPlay？比原版售价 99 美元贵了 50 美元，苹果甚至没有升级音响系统。感觉就像公司给这个打电话了。现在我已经拿到了几个并将它们放在我的家庭办公室里，我更加热情了。 Mini 2 比第一代 Mini 快得多，可以在几秒钟内播放音乐，并同样快速地响应智能家居命令。如果您厌倦了站在 HomePod 旁等待它最终完成您要求的操作，那么仅此一点就值得升级。以下是我在使用新款 Mini 2 几天后最喜欢的三个功能，以及令我非常失望的一个功能。 [图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268839_HomePod_mini_2_JTuohy_0015.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Siri 更加敏捷且不那么健谈 Mini 2 最大的升级是 Siri AI，但目前尚未推出。苹果表示，它将在软件更新中“稍后”推出。不过，基础的智能语音助手确实有了进步。 Mini 2 上的 Siri 比第一代 Mini 上的 Siri 更快，通常会在三秒内做出响应。这要归功于更新、更快的处理器（S10，从 S5 升级）和 Wi-Fi 6E 支持（从 Wi-Fi 4 升级）。当我让 Siri 播放泰勒·斯威夫特 (Taylor Swift) 时，几秒钟后一首歌曲开始播放。它在两秒内正确地告诉我谁赢得了今年的世界职业棒球大赛，并在三秒内关掉灯或打开百叶窗。 [视频：HomePod Mini2 与 Mini 1 智能家居速度]这是一个巨大的进步
